round: review-response hardening of merged PR #772 (upstream c3259492, merge 6a9690c3)
metric: assembly byte-comparison plus instruction and stack-reference counts. Static; no PMU, no cycles, no Raptor Lake.

corpora.name: tests/regression (each file with its own .flags)
corpora.note: 1 skip is a file whose .flags this host cannot satisfy. An earlier run reported compared=830 skipped=15; the 14 extra skips were the -m32 legs failing for want of 32-bit glibc headers (INF-M32HDRS-1), and installing gcc-multilib/libc6-dev-i386 raised coverage to 844 with the verdict unchanged. Four -fprofile-generate=@PROFDIR@ files initially reported as changed; a self-A/B of ONE binary against itself reproduced the difference, which is the PID baked into the .profraw name and the __lccc_pgo_dump_<hash>_<pid> symbol. Normalised in the harness.

corpora.name: tests/bench (12 k_*.c performance kernels) + tests/benchmark/kernel_corpus (24) + tests/benchmark/patterns (3)
corpora.note: Added last and is the most important row: it contains k_varint.c, the kernel the merged IVSR-PTRADD-1 win was measured on, plus the extracted real-workload files. Byte-identical assembly on all twelve kernels means the instruction stream is identical, so Callgrind Ir is identical and no dynamic re-run was needed - that is an inference from the static result, not a skipped measurement.

pid_nondeterminism.finding: -fprofile-generate=@PROFDIR@ output is not reproducible run to run: the literal @PROFDIR@ template is replaced with a name containing the PID, emitted both as a .byte list and as __lccc_pgo_dump_<hash>_<pid>.
pid_nondeterminism.proof: the SAME binary compiled the SAME source twice and produced different assembly (99551.profraw vs 99557.profraw).
pid_nondeterminism.consequence: any assembly A/B over tests/regression reports 4 phantom changes unless it normalises them. ab_regression.py now does.

A3_is_used_as_address_narrowing.proposal: replace IntrinsicOp::reads_pointer_arg() with may_read_memory() in is_used_as_address, on the grounds that the read-only allowlist over-approximates (it is true for pure vector arithmetic) and over-approximation is the unsafe direction for an address test.

measured.note: one instruction smaller but structurally worse: lost the hoisted pointer recurrence and a 17-instruction unrolled byte-sum

A3_is_used_as_address_narrowing.mechanism: the hoisted recurrence `leaq 16(%r9), %r9` was replaced by a per-iteration `movslq %r8d,%r9; leaq -272(%rbp),%rdi; leaq (%rdi,%r9,4),%rdi` re-derivation, plus an xmm spill/reload pair where the value previously stayed in a register (`movdqa %xmm0,%xmm4` became `movdqu %xmm0,-304(%rbp)` + `movdqu -304(%rbp),%xmm1`).
A3_is_used_as_address_narrowing.verdict: REVERTED. The soundness argument for the wide predicate is positive: the classification can only arm a recurrence on a value that try_lower_pointer_arithmetic already put in POINTER-width arithmetic, where the integer and pointer rings agree for every program without UB (a wrapping base+i*elem is UB in the source per C17 6.5.6p8). Narrow-ring products are guarded separately by offset_product_cannot_overflow.
